name: Newsletters » Topics » Media » Wikipedia
comments: Imported from Thunderbird msgFilterRules.dat (commit ea19cd6)
2026-08-17: merged the separate 'Newsletters » Topics » Media » Wikipedia'
rule (253470659_newsletters_wikipedia.json, matched @lists.wikimedia.org) into
this one so all Wikipedia mail lands in one place under a single rule.
'@lists.wikimedia.org' as a contains match already covers
'daily-article-l@lists.wikimedia.org', so that condition was dropped in favor
of the broader one; 'hello@wikimedia.org' was kept since it's not a lists.wikimedia.org
address. Took the higher priority (100) of the two merged rules.
2026-08-17: added Economist-style age brackets -- two mutually exclusive age
brackets partition every possible age, so this rule always matches once
conditions match (no plain actions mixed in, avoiding a double-queue risk).
Re-evaluated by the weekly --all-folders resweep, which is the only mechanism
that revisits mail already filed outside INBOX.
2026-08-21: merged 1746400087_charity_wikimedia.json into this rule (same
destination folder). Simplified conditions to a single bare '@wikimedia.org'
contains match, which is a strict superset of the previous
'@lists.wikimedia.org' / 'hello@wikimedia.org' pair.
2026-08-23: BUG FIX -- the 2026-08-21 'strict superset' claim was wrong.
'contains' is a literal substring match, not a domain-aware one, and
'@wikimedia.org' is NOT a substring of 'daily-article-l@lists.wikimedia.org'
(the '@' there is followed by 'lists', not 'wikimedia'). This silently
broke matching for all *@lists.wikimedia.org senders. Changed the match
value to bare 'wikimedia.org' (no leading '@'), which is a true substring
of both 'hello@wikimedia.org' and '...@lists.wikimedia.org'.
